Depuis le 9 janvier 2024, des nouvelles: Since January 9, 2024, new measures have been in effect for admitting Palestinians from the Gaza Strip to Canada. One thousand of them can be admitted, which has set off a true race against the clock, according to Palestinians in Canada. They feel they are being treated differently, as the situation of their loved ones in the Gaza Strip deteriorates after more than 100 days of war in the Palestinian enclave. Time is running out for them: their families in Gaza must flee bombings, death, famine, disease and thirst.
Dalya Shaat fait bouillir de l’eau pour: Dalya Shaat boils water to make coffee. “Everything here is from Gaza,” says the master’s student in mental health and social justice, pointing to the decorations in her Montréal apartment. “Like this coffee pot in the middle of the table,” she says. They are all keepsakes she brought back from her last trip to Gaza, in 2022, when she volunteered at a hospital with children who are hard of hearing.
Elle montre un sachet de café qui porte: She holds up a packet of coffee bearing the logo of a small company, Babaroti. “It was the family’s coffee. Now it’s destroyed, in ruins,” says Dalya, shaking her head. “Even taking a bite of chocolate makes me feel guilty today.” She has been trying to bring family members over since the temporary resident visa (TRV) program opened.
Ce visa permet aux ressortissants palest: This visa allows Palestinian nationals to stay in Canada for three years if their family supports them financially. An ordeal, she says, and a heavy blow to absorb.

Lorsque la Russie a envahi l’Ukraine, le: When Russia invaded Ukraine, Canada quickly set up a welcome program, the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET), which came into effect in March 2022. « Les gens doivent payer 100 $ par deman: “People have to pay $100 per application, or $500 for a family of more than five people.” “(Immigration Canada) made an exception by processing the applications of more than a million Ukrainians free of charge, yet they can’t waive the application fees for 1,000 Palestinians!” – one more piece of evidence of a two-tier treatment, according to the lawyer.
